records.summary: 414 Columbus Ave sits in the North Beach NCD where restaurants serving alcohol on the first story require Conditional Use Authorization under both the base zoning district (§ 722) and the North Beach Special Use District (§ 780.3). The property has operated continuously as a restaurant since at least 1986, with an active ABC Type 41 license since 2016. The site history shows three Conditional Use approvals (1986, 1998, 2010) to upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47, add live entertainment, and add amplified music. The neighborhood is exceptionally dense: 60 food and drink businesses within 500 feet, 40 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet, and 97 within 1,000 feet. Despite high density, recent approvals nearby show the Planning Department routinely approves Type 41 and Type 47 upgrades for existing restaurants as continuations of use.

patterns.pattern: Recent (2021) agency referrals for Type 41 and Type 47 on the Columbus Avenue corridor in North Beach NCD uniformly approved as continuations of existing restaurant use, provided the operator maintains a bona fide eating place, with no extracted conditions.

When an existing restaurant with a prior CUA seeks ABC referral for Type 47 continuation or transfer, Planning approves it as an agency referral (not a new use decision), citing the prior approval and §722/§780.3. This pattern appears at 431 Columbus (2017, 2018) and 1512 Stockton (2019).

North Beach SUD policy shifted in 2020 (Ordinance 182-20) to permit certain restaurants and eating places without CUA or public notice if they operated as bona fide eating places, liberalizing approval for existing food businesses. This ordinance is cited in multiple 2021 referrals as the basis for approval.

All agency referrals for alcohol licenses at existing restaurants in North Beach NCD since 2017 in this candidate set were approved, with Planning citing §722 and §780.3 and requiring the operator to maintain the premises as a bona fide eating place. No denials appear in the record.

Restaurants on the 400 block of Columbus (411, 414, 431 Columbus) have been approved for alcohol service (Type 41 and Type 47) multiple times between 2017–2021, all as continuations of existing use with no discretionary hearing required.

approvals.summary: Intensifying the existing restaurant with a full-liquor license requires a Conditional Use Authorization in the North Beach NCD and Special Use District, per Planning Code § 722 and § 780.3(c)(2)(A), with a finding that the restaurant is and will remain a bona fide eating place.

findings.text: An active ABC Type 41 (beer and wine, eating place) license has been on file at 414 Columbus Ave since March 2016, and the site has operated as a restaurant continuously since at least 1986.

Planning approved three Conditional Use Authorizations at this address: upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 in February 1987, adding live entertainment in July 1998, and adding amplified music in November 2010.

North Beach Special Use District § 780.3(c)(2)(A) requires restaurants serving full liquor to obtain Conditional Use Authorization and a Commission finding that the restaurant is and will remain a bona fide eating place, demonstrated by maintaining at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared and sold on premises.

Planning Code § 178 prohibits significantly altering, enlarging, or intensifying a conditional use without a new Conditional Use Authorization; upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 intensifies the alcohol service at an existing conditionally approved restaurant.

All recent (2017–2021) agency referrals for Type 41 and Type 47 licenses at existing restaurants on Columbus Avenue and nearby Grant Avenue in North Beach NCD were approved by Planning as continuations of use, provided the restaurant operates as a bona fide eating place.
The description does not say whether the business is part of a chain or whether it amends conditions of the three earlier CUAs, so the rules could not decide those questions.

approvals.summary: The Type 47 license requires a premises-to-premises transfer and ABC investigation, and census tract 106.00 is over-concentrated (52 active on-sale licenses against 12 authorized), so a public convenience or necessity finding is likely required.

findings.text: Type 47 is a quota license under California Business and Professions Code § 23816; San Francisco County exceeds its population quota, so the license must be acquired by purchasing and transferring an existing one.

Census tract 106.00 held 52 active on-sale retail licenses on March 9, 2022, against 12 authorized in ABC's September 2026 census tract authorizations, triggering the undue-concentration test under Business and Professions Code § 23958.4.

When a census tract is over its authorized number, state law tests a premises-to-premises transfer for undue concentration; the license may still issue if public convenience or necessity would be served.
ABC will refer the application to the Police Department (ABC Liaison Unit) and the Planning Department for review under Business and Professions Code § 23987.
The North Beach Special Use District requires Conditional Use Authorization for a restaurant to serve full liquor, so the license can be used only with a CUA from Planning.

expected_conditions.condition: The restaurant must operate and maintain the premises as a bona fide eating place, with at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared and sold on the premises, and provide sales records to Planning on request.
expected_conditions.basis: North Beach SUD § 780.3(c)(2)(A) requires restaurants serving full liquor to demonstrate they are bona fide eating places with at least 51% food receipts. All recent (2017–2021) Type 47 referrals in the comparable set cite this requirement and the need to maintain it.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of alcohol service limited to no later than 2 a.m., consistent with state law and North Beach NCD § 722, which treats hours after 2 a.m. as not principally permitted.
expected_conditions.basis: California law prohibits on-sale alcohol service after 2 a.m., and Planning Code § 722 treats hours after 2 a.m. in North Beach NCD as not principally permitted. Comparable CUAs in North Beach typically condition alcohol service to end by 2 a.m.

expected_conditions.condition: The use may not be further enlarged, altered, or intensified without a new Conditional Use Authorization, per Planning Code § 178.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 178 is a standard condition on all conditional uses in San Francisco, prohibiting significant alteration or intensification without returning to the Commission.

expected_conditions.condition: Compliance with a good-neighbor policy addressing noise, litter, and patron behavior, and a contact for neighborhood complaints.
expected_conditions.basis: Recent restaurant and bar CUAs in dense neighborhoods commonly include good-neighbor commitments as conditions. The North Beach area is exceptionally dense (60 food and drink businesses within 500 feet), so the Commission is likely to impose operational conditions to mitigate impacts.

expected_conditions.condition: The authorization is valid for three years from the effective date; DBI must issue a building or site permit to commence the use within that period.
expected_conditions.basis: This is a standard validity condition on all San Francisco CUAs under Planning Code § 186, appearing in the conditions extracted from comparable case 2019-004021CUA.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the zoning pathway in writing with San Francisco Planning before filing or paying for anything.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting or a written zoning determination from Planning to confirm: (1) that intensifying the restaurant by upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 requires a new Conditional Use Authorization under § 178 and § 780.3(c)(2)(A); (2) whether the proposal amends conditions of the three earlier CUAs (1986, 1998, 2010) and thus requires review under § 303(e); (3) what documentation Planning will require to demonstrate the restaurant meets the bona fide eating place standard (51% food sales); and (4) whether a Public Convenience or Necessity letter will be needed for ABC given the census tract over-concentration. Bring the sales records for the preceding year and the description of the proposed operation.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a CUA is required, file the Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning, including the ABC transfer documents, sales records, and a narrative addressing the § 303 findings.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The application narrative should frame the proposal as intensifying an existing, long-established restaurant (operating since 1986 with three prior CUAs) by upgrading the alcohol license to better serve patrons. Emphasize that the restaurant will continue to operate as a bona fide eating place with at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared on site, and provide sales records demonstrating compliance. Address the § 303 findings, particularly that the use is necessary or desirable for the neighborhood (supporting an established local business), will not be detrimental to nearby properties, and serves the public convenience. Note that recent comparable restaurants on Columbus Avenue and nearby streets obtained Type 47 approvals as continuations of use without opposition. Submit neighborhood outreach documentation (letters of support from adjacent businesses or residents, if availabl…

filing_playbook.action: Conduct the mandatory pre-application community meeting and post the 300-foot notice for the required period before the Planning Commission hearing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At the community meeting, present the proposal as a modest upgrade of an existing restaurant that has served the neighborhood for decades, emphasizing continued food service as the primary use and the commitment to the 51% food-sales requirement. Address neighbor concerns about noise, hours, and patron behavior, and commit to a good-neighbor policy with a contact for complaints. Document attendance and any feedback to submit with the CUA application.

filing_playbook.action: After CUA approval, apply to ABC for the premises-to-premises transfer of the Type 47 license, submitting the executed lease, seller's permit, entity registration, signed purchase agreement for the license, and Planning's CUA approval.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Include in the ABC application: the CUA approval from Planning, documentation that the restaurant is a bona fide eating place (menu, sales records showing at least 51% food receipts), a floor plan, a statement of the operational concept, and the executed escrow for the license purchase. Request that Planning provide ABC a Public Convenience or Necessity letter supporting the transfer in the over-concentrated census tract, citing the restaurant's long history at this address, its contribution to the neighborhood, and the CUA approval. Submit the 30-day public posting affidavit after the notice period expires.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for or renew the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, the health permit to operate, and the fictitious business name statement (if the DBA differs from the legal entity name).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register the business with the Treasurer & Tax Collector immediately after forming the entity (or confirm the existing registration is current). Apply for the health permit after the kitchen plans are approved by DPH's plan check, and schedule the pre-opening inspection once construction (if any) is substantially complete. File the fictitious business name statement with the County Clerk if the restaurant operates as 'Mona Lisa Mare e Monti' but the legal entity has a different name, and publish it in an approved newspaper within 45 days.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline: The range is 120–300 days to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization and the ABC Type 47 license transfer when both are granted. The CUA process in North Beach NCD typically takes 4–6 months from filing to hearing, including the mandatory pre-application meeting, 300-foot notice, and the 30-day appeal period after approval. The ABC premises-to-premises transfer takes 90–180 days including escrow, posting, police and Planning referrals, and undue-concentration review; an over-concentrated census tract requiring a Public Convenience or Necessity finding adds 1–3 months to the ABC timeline. The two processes run partly in parallel (ABC referral to Planning occurs during the CUA review), but ABC will not issue the license until the CUA is final and the appeal period has expired. Cost: The range is $20,150–$453,850. The Type 47 license purchase is the largest variable: $17,000–$450,000 depending on the seller's asking price for an existing license in San Francisco, plus $1,000–$1,600 ABC transfer fee. The CUA filing fee was about $2,747 (no-construction) in 2023–24 and is CPI-adjusted annually (approximately $3,100–$3,500 in 2022 dollars). Health permit application is $470, business registration $55–$700 depending on gross receipts, and other state/city registrations total approximately $300–$600. Music licensing (ASCAP, BMI) is $600–$5,000 annually but is not a government fee and is excluded from this range. If no building permit is needed (no construction stated), omit DBI, Fire, and FOG permit costs. These figures are for the approvals in the entitlement path when granted; they are not a time or cost to a denial or withdrawal.
